mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient over triggered periods is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months, in the absence of a simultaneous GDP contraction (GDPC1), signals labor-market softening without broad economic collapse, which historically precedes mild equity pullbacks over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 not falling YoY
candidate_failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation is simultaneously rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is stable or falling indicates supply-side disruption without labor-market slack, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND UNRATE monthly change >= -0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >1.5pp in one month to below 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed outside of crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its previous peak, combined with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals a tight labor market without cost-push pressures, which historically supports positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous peak AND CPIAUCSL monthly change within ±0.2%
regime_hint: tight labor market with stable prices
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears when wage growth accelerates sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 10% while consumer spending (GDPC1) is flat signals a precautionary savings surge, which typically precedes equity pullbacks as consumers delay discretionary purchases over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 10% AND GDPC1 monthly change within ±0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present when monetary policy is simultaneously expansionary.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 8% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to correlated construction-sector and material equities outperformance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant over a 10-year walk-forward test.
